asma: Dhu Al Jalaali Wa Al Ikraam

dhikr.ar: قال رسول الله ﷺ: «أَيَعْجِزُ أَحَدُكُمْ أَنْ يَكْسِبَ كُلَّ يَوْمٍ أَلْفَ حَسَنَةٍ. فَسَأَلَهُ سَائِلٌ مِنْ جُلَسَائِهِ كَيْفَ يَكْسِبُ أَحَدُنَا أَلْفَ حَسَنَةٍ قَالَ يُسَبِّحُ مِائَةَ تَسْبِيحَةٍ فَيُكْتَبُ لَهُ أَلْفُ حَسَنَةٍ أَوْ يُحَطُّ عَنْهُ أَلْفُ خَطِيئَةٍ»
dhikr.en: Is one amongst you powerless to get one thousand virtues every day. Amongst those who had been sitting there, one asked: How one amongst us can get one thousand virtues every day? He said: Recite:" Hallowed be Allah" one hundred times for (by reciting them) one thousand virtues are recorded (to your credit) and one tbousand vices are blotted out

dhikr.ar: قال رسول الله ﷺ: «وَالْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ تَمْلأُ الْمِيزَانَ. وَسُبْحَانَ اللَّهِ وَالْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ تَمْلآنِ - أَوْ تَمْلأُ - مَا بَيْنَ السَّمَوَاتِ وَالأَرْضِ»
dhikr.en: al-Hamdu Lillah (all praise and gratitude is for Allah alone) fills the scale, and Subhan Allah (Glory be to Allah) and al-Hamdu Lillah fill up what is between the heavens and the earth

dhikr.ar: قال رسول الله ﷺ: «مَنْ سَبَّحَ اللَّهَ فِي دُبُرِ كُلِّ صَلاَةٍ ثَلاَثًا وَثَلاَثِينَ وَحَمِدَ اللَّهَ ثَلاَثًا وَثَلاَثِينَ وَكَبَّرَ اللَّهَ ثَلاَثًا وَثَلاَثِينَ فَتِلْكَ تِسْعَةٌ وَتِسْعُونَ وَقَالَ تَمَامَ الْمِائَةِ لاَ إِلَهَ إِلاَّ اللَّهُ وَحْدَهُ لاَ شَرِيكَ لَهُ لَهُ الْمُلْكُ وَلَهُ الْحَمْدُ وَهُوَ عَلَى كُلِّ شَىْءٍ قَدِيرٌ غُفِرَتْ خَطَايَاهُ وَإِنْ كَانَتْ مِثْلَ زَبَدِ الْبَحْرِ»
dhikr.en: If anyone extols Allah after every prayer thirty-three times, and praises Allah thirty-three times, and declares His Greatness thirty-three times, ninety-nine times in all, and says to complete a hundred:" There is no god but Allah, having no partner with Him, to Him belongs sovereignty and to Him is praise due, and He is Potent over everything," his sins will be forgiven even If these are as abundant as the foam of the sea

dhikr.ar: قال رسول الله ﷺ: «أَحَبُّ الْكَلاَمِ إِلَى اللَّهِ أَرْبَعٌ سُبْحَانَ اللَّهِ وَالْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ وَلاَ إِلَهَ إِلاَّ اللَّهُ وَاللَّهُ أَكْبَرُ. لاَ يَضُرُّكَ بَأَيِّهِنَّ بَدَأْتَ»
dhikr.en: The dearest phrases to Allah are four: Subhan Allah (Hallowed be Allah), Al-Hamdulillah (Praise be to Allah), La ilaha illa-Allah (There is no deity but Allah), Allahu Akbar (Allah is Greater). There is no harm for you in which of them begin with

dhikr.en: The best remembrance is: ‘there is none worthy of worship except Allah (Lā ilāha illallāh)’ and the best supplication is: ‘All praise is due to Allah (Al-ḥamdulillāh).

dhikr.ar: قال رسول الله ﷺ: «لأَنْ أَقُولَ سُبْحَانَ اللَّهِ وَالْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ وَلاَ إِلَهَ إِلاَّ اللَّهُ وَاللَّهُ أَكْبَرُ أَحَبُّ إِلَىَّ مِمَّا طَلَعَتْ عَلَيْهِ الشَّمْسُ»
dhikr.en: The uttering of (these words):" Hallowed be Allah; all praise is due to Allah, there is no god but Allah and Allah is the Greatest," is dearer to me than anything over which the sun rises

dhikr.ar: قال رسول الله ﷺ: «مَنْ سَبَّحَ اللَّهَ فِي دُبُرِ كُلِّ صَلاَةٍ ثَلاَثًا وَثَلاَثِينَ وَحَمِدَ اللَّهَ ثَلاَثًا وَثَلاَثِينَ وَكَبَّرَ اللَّهَ ثَلاَثًا وَثَلاَثِينَ فَتِلْكَ تِسْعَةٌ وَتِسْعُونَ وَقَالَ تَمَامَ الْمِائَةِ لاَ إِلَهَ إِلاَّ اللَّهُ وَحْدَهُ لاَ شَرِيكَ لَهُ لَهُ الْمُلْكُ وَلَهُ الْحَمْدُ وَهُوَ عَلَى كُلِّ شَىْءٍ قَدِيرٌ غُفِرَتْ خَطَايَاهُ وَإِنْ كَانَتْ مِثْلَ زَبَدِ الْبَحْرِ»

dhikr: None has the right to be worshipped except Allah

dhikr.ar: قال رسول الله ﷺ: «أَفْضَلُ الذِّكْرِ لاَ إِلَهَ إِلاَّ اللَّهُ وَأَفْضَلُ الدُّعَاءِ الْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ»
dhikr.en: The best remembrance is: ‘there is none worthy of worship except Allah (Lā ilāha illallāh)’ and the best supplication is: ‘All praise is due to Allah (Al-ḥamdulillāh).

dhikr.ar: قال رسول الله ﷺ: «أَحَبُّ الْكَلاَمِ إِلَى اللَّهِ أَرْبَعٌ سُبْحَانَ اللَّهِ وَالْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ وَلاَ إِلَهَ إِلاَّ اللَّهُ وَاللَّهُ أَكْبَرُ. لاَ يَضُرُّكَ بَأَيِّهِنَّ بَدَأْتَ»
dhikr.en: The dearest phrases to Allah are four: Subhan Allah (Hallowed be Allah), Al-Hamdulillah (Praise be to Allah), La ilaha illa-Allah (There is no deity but Allah), Allahu Akbar (Allah is Greater). There is no harm for you in which of them begin with

dhikr.ar: قال رسول الله ﷺ: «إِنَّهُ لَيُغَانُ عَلَى قَلْبِي وَإِنِّي لأَسْتَغْفِرُ اللَّهَ فِي الْيَوْمِ مِائَةَ مَرَّةٍ»
dhikr.en: There is (at times) some sort of shade upon my heart, and I seek forgiveness from Allah a hundred times a day

dhikr.ar: قال رسول الله ﷺ: «وَاللَّهِ إِنِّي لأَسْتَغْفِرُ اللَّهَ وَأَتُوبُ إِلَيْهِ فِي الْيَوْمِ أَكْثَرَ مِنْ سَبْعِينَ مَرَّةً»
dhikr.en: By Allah! I ask for forgiveness from Allah and turn to Him in repentance more than seventy times a day

dhikr.ar: فَقُلْتُ اسْتَغْفِرُوا رَبَّكُمْ إِنَّهُ كَانَ غَفَّارًا ۝ يُرْسِلِ السَّمَاءَ عَلَيْكُم مِّدْرَارًا ۝ وَيُمْدِدْكُم بِأَمْوَالٍ وَبَنِينَ وَيَجْعَل لَّكُمْ جَنَّاتٍ وَيَجْعَل لَّكُمْ أَنْهَارًا
dhikr.en: And said, 'Ask forgiveness of your Lord. Indeed, He is ever a Perpetual Forgiver. He will send [rain from] the sky upon you in [continuing] showers And give you increase in wealth and children and provide for you gardens and provide for you rivers.

dhikr: O Allah, send blessings upon Muhammad

dhikr.ar: قال رسول الله ﷺ: «مَنْ صَلَّى عَلَىَّ وَاحِدَةً صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ عَشْرًا»
dhikr.en: He who blesses me once, Allah would bless him ten times

dhikr: La hawla wa la quwwata illa billah
لاَ حَوْلَ وَلاَ قُوَّةَ إِلاَّ بِاللَّهِ
La hawla wa la quwwata illa billah
There is no might nor power except with Allah

dhikr.ar: قال رسول الله ﷺ لأبي موسى رضي الله عنه: «يَا عَبْدَ اللَّهِ بْنَ قَيْسٍ قُلْ لاَ حَوْلَ وَلاَ قُوَّةَ إِلاَّ بِاللَّهِ فَإِنَّهَا. كَنْزٌ مِنْ كُنُوزِ الْجَنَّةِ»
dhikr.en: O `Abdullah bin Qais! Say: La haul a walaquwata illa bil-lah, for it is one of the treasures of Paradise

dhikr: Glory be to Allah and praise be to Him

dhikr.ar: قال رسول الله ﷺ: «مَنْ قَالَ سُبْحَانَ اللَّهِ وَبِحَمْدِهِ. فِي يَوْمٍ مِائَةَ مَرَّةٍ حُطَّتْ خَطَايَاهُ، وَإِنْ كَانَتْ مِثْلَ زَبَدِ الْبَحْرِ»
dhikr.en: Whoever says, 'Subhan Allah wa bihamdihi,' one hundred times a day, will be forgiven all his sins even if they were as much as the foam of the sea

dhikr.ar: قال رسول الله ﷺ: «كَلِمَتَانِ خَفِيفَتَانِ عَلَى اللِّسَانِ، ثَقِيلَتَانِ فِي الْمِيزَانِ، حَبِيبَتَانِ إِلَى الرَّحْمَنِ، سُبْحَانَ اللَّهِ الْعَظِيمِ، سُبْحَانَ اللَّهِ وَبِحَمْدِهِ»
dhikr.en: There are two expressions which are very easy for the tongue to say, but they are very heavy in the balance and are very dear to The Beneficent (Allah), and they are, 'Subhan Allah Al- `Azim and 'Subhan Allah wa bihamdihi

dhikr: Glory be to Allah, the Most Great, and praise be to Him

dhikr.ar: قال رسول الله ﷺ: «مَنْ قَالَ سُبْحَانَ اللَّهِ الْعَظِيمِ وَبِحَمْدِهِ. غُرِسَتْ لَهُ نَخْلَةٌ فِي الْجَنَّةِ»
dhikr.en: Whoever says: ‘Glory is to Allah, the Magnificent, and with His Praise (Subḥān Allāhil-Aẓīm, wa biḥamdih)’ a date-palm tree is planted for him in Paradise.

dhikr.ar: قال رسول الله ﷺ: «كَلِمَتَانِ خَفِيفَتَانِ عَلَى اللِّسَانِ، ثَقِيلَتَانِ فِي الْمِيزَانِ، حَبِيبَتَانِ إِلَى الرَّحْمَنِ، سُبْحَانَ اللَّهِ الْعَظِيمِ، سُبْحَانَ اللَّهِ وَبِحَمْدِهِ»
dhikr.en: There are two expressions which are very easy for the tongue to say, but they are very heavy in the balance and are very dear to The Beneficent (Allah), and they are, 'Subhan Allah Al- `Azim and 'Subhan Allah wa bihamdihi

dhikr: La ilaha illallahu wahdahu… (100× a day)
لاَ إِلَهَ إِلاَّ اللَّهُ وَحْدَهُ لاَ شَرِيكَ لَهُ، لَهُ الْمُلْكُ، وَلَهُ الْحَمْدُ، وَهُوَ عَلَى كُلِّ شَيْءٍ قَدِيرٌ
La ilaha illallahu wahdahu la sharika lah, lahul-mulku wa lahul-hamd, wa huwa 'ala kulli shay'in qadir
None has the right to be worshipped except Allah, alone, without partner. His is the dominion and His is the praise, and He is over all things capable

dhikr.ar: قال رسول الله ﷺ: «مَنْ قَالَ لاَ إِلَهَ إِلاَّ اللَّهُ وَحْدَهُ لاَ شَرِيكَ لَهُ، لَهُ الْمُلْكُ، وَلَهُ الْحَمْدُ، وَهُوَ عَلَى كُلِّ شَىْءٍ قَدِيرٌ. فِي يَوْمٍ مِائَةَ مَرَّةٍ، كَانَتْ لَهُ عَدْلَ عَشْرِ رِقَابٍ، وَكُتِبَتْ لَهُ مِائَةُ حَسَنَةٍ، وَمُحِيَتْ عَنْهُ مِائَةُ سَيِّئَةٍ، وَكَانَتْ لَهُ حِرْزًا مِنَ الشَّيْطَانِ يَوْمَهُ ذَلِكَ حَتَّى يُمْسِيَ، وَلَمْ يَأْتِ أَحَدٌ بِأَفْضَلَ مِمَّا جَاءَ بِهِ، إِلاَّ أَحَدٌ عَمِلَ أَكْثَرَ مِنْ ذَلِكَ»
dhikr.en: If one says one-hundred times in one day: "None has the right to be worshipped but Allah, the Alone Who has no partners, to Him belongs Dominion and to Him belong all the Praises, and He has power over all things (i.e. Omnipotent)", one will get the reward of manumitting ten slaves, and one-hundred good deeds will be written in his account, and one-hundred bad deeds will be wiped off or erased from his account, and on that day he will be protected from the morning till evening from Satan, and nobody will be superior to him except one who has done more than that which he has done

dhikr.ar: قال رسول الله ﷺ: «أَفْضَلُ الذِّكْرِ لاَ إِلَهَ إِلاَّ اللَّهُ وَأَفْضَلُ الدُّعَاءِ الْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ»
dhikr.en: The best remembrance is: ‘there is none worthy of worship except Allah (Lā ilāha illallāh)’ and the best supplication is: ‘All praise is due to Allah (Al-ḥamdulillāh).

events.ar: قال رسول الله ﷺ: «أَفْضَلُ الصِّيَامِ بَعْدَ رَمَضَانَ شَهْرُ اللَّهِ الْمُحَرَّمُ وَأَفْضَلُ الصَّلاَةِ بَعْدَ الْفَرِيضَةِ صَلاَةُ اللَّيْلِ»
events.en: The most excellent fast after Ramadan is God's month. al-Muharram, and the most excellent prayer after what is prescribed is prayer during the night
events.title: Fast often in Muharram

events.ar: عن النبي ﷺ: «وَسُئِلَ عَنْ صَوْمِ يَوْمِ عَاشُورَاءَ فَقَالَ يُكَفِّرُ السَّنَةَ الْمَاضِيَةَ»
events.en: He was asked about fasting on the day of 'Ashura (10th of Muharram), whereupon be said: It expiates the sins of the preceding year.
events.title: Fast the 10th of Muharram

events.ar: قال رسول الله ﷺ: «فَإِذَا كَانَ الْعَامُ الْمُقْبِلُ - إِنْ شَاءَ اللَّهُ - صُمْنَا الْيَوْمَ التَّاسِعَ»
events.en: When the next year comes, God willing, we would observe fast on the 9th
events.title: Also fast the 9th

events.ar: قال رسول الله ﷺ: «مَنْ صَامَ رَمَضَانَ إِيمَانًا وَاحْتِسَابًا غُفِرَ لَهُ مَا تَقَدَّمَ مِنْ ذَنْبِهِ»
events.en: Whoever observes fasts during the month of Ramadan out of sincere faith, and hoping to attain Allah's rewards, then all his past sins will be forgiven
events.title: Fast with faith and hope of reward

events.ar: قال رسول الله ﷺ: «مَنْ قَامَ لَيْلَةَ الْقَدْرِ إِيمَانًا وَاحْتِسَابًا غُفِرَ لَهُ مَا تَقَدَّمَ مِنْ ذَنْبِهِ»
events.en: Whoever established prayers on the night of Qadr out of sincere faith and hoping for a reward from Allah, then all his previous sins will be forgiven
events.title: Pray at night

events.ar: قال رسول الله ﷺ لعائشة رضي الله عنها: «قُولِي اللَّهُمَّ إِنَّكَ عَفُوٌّ كَرِيمٌ تُحِبُّ الْعَفْوَ فَاعْفُ عَنِّي»
events.en: Say: “O Allah, indeed You are Pardoning, [Generous,] You love pardon, so pardon me
events.title: The dua for Laylat al-Qadr

events.ar: عن ابن عمر رضي الله عنهما: «فَرَضَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ ﷺ زَكَاةَ الْفِطْرِ صَاعًا مِنْ تَمْرٍ، أَوْ صَاعًا مِنْ شَعِيرٍ عَلَى الْعَبْدِ وَالْحُرِّ، وَالذَّكَرِ وَالأُنْثَى، وَالصَّغِيرِ وَالْكَبِيرِ مِنَ الْمُسْلِمِينَ، وَأَمَرَ بِهَا أَنْ تُؤَدَّى قَبْلَ خُرُوجِ النَّاسِ إِلَى الصَّلاَةِ»
events.en: Allah's Messenger (peace be upon him) enjoined the payment of one Sa' of dates or one Sa' of barley as Zakat-ul-Fitr on every Muslim slave or free, male or female, young or old, and he ordered that it be paid before the people went out to offer the `Id prayer
events.title: Pay Zakat al-Fitr before the Eid prayer

events.ar: عن أنس رضي الله عنه: «كَانَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ ﷺ لاَ يَغْدُو يَوْمَ الْفِطْرِ حَتَّى يَأْكُلَ تَمَرَاتٍ»
events.en: Allah's Messenger (peace be upon him) never proceeded (for the prayer) on the Day of `Id-ul-Fitr unless he had eaten some dates
events.title: Eat some dates before going out

events.ar: قال رسول الله ﷺ: «مَنْ صَامَ رَمَضَانَ ثُمَّ أَتْبَعَهُ سِتًّا مِنْ شَوَّالٍ كَانَ كَصِيَامِ الدَّهْرِ»
events.en: He who observed the fast of Ramadan and then followed it with six (fasts) of Shawwal. it would be as if he fasted perpetually
events.title: Fast six days of Shawwal

events: First ten days of Dhul Hijjah

events.ar: قال رسول الله ﷺ: «مَا الْعَمَلُ فِي أَيَّامِ الْعَشْرِ أَفْضَلَ مِنَ الْعَمَلِ فِي هَذِهِ»
events.en: No good deeds done on other days are superior to those done on these (first ten days of Dhul Hijja)
events.title: Do extra good deeds

events.ar: عن النبي ﷺ: «وَسُئِلَ عَنْ صَوْمِ يَوْمِ عَرَفَةَ فَقَالَ يُكَفِّرُ السَّنَةَ الْمَاضِيَةَ وَالْبَاقِيَةَ»
events.en: He was asked about fasting on the day of 'Arafa (9th of Dhu'I-Hijja), whereupon he said: It expiates the sins of the preceding year and the coming year.
events.title: Fast the Day of Arafah (if not on Hajj)
When sacrificing, say
events.ar: بِسْمِ اللَّهِ وَاللَّهُ أَكْبَرُ اللَّهُمَّ مِنْكَ وَلَكَ اللَّهُمَّ تَقَبَّلْ مِنِّي
events.en: In the name of Allah, and Allah is the greatest. O Allah, (it is) from You and belongs to You, O Allah, accept this from me.

events.ar: قال رسول الله ﷺ: «أَيَّامُ التَّشْرِيقِ أَيَّامُ أَكْلٍ وَشُرْبٍ»
events.en: The days of Tashriq are the days of eating and drinking
events.title: Days of eating and drinking

events.ar: قال رسول الله ﷺ: «صِيَامُ ثَلاَثَةِ أَيَّامٍ مِنْ كُلِّ شَهْرٍ صِيَامُ الدَّهْرِ وَأَيَّامُ الْبِيضِ صَبِيحَةَ ثَلاَثَ عَشْرَةَ وَأَرْبَعَ عَشْرَةَ وَخَمْسَ عَشْرَةَ»
events.en: Fasting three days of each month is fasting for a lifetime, and the shining days of Al-Bid, the thirteenth, fourteenth and fifteenth
events.title: Fast the 13th, 14th and 15th

events.ar: عن أبي هريرة رضي الله عنه: «أَوْصَانِي خَلِيلِي ﷺ بِثَلاَثٍ صِيَامِ ثَلاَثَةِ أَيَّامٍ مِنْ كُلِّ شَهْرٍ، وَرَكْعَتَىِ الضُّحَى، وَأَنْ أُوتِرَ قَبْلَ أَنْ أَنَامَ»
events.en: My friend (the Prophet (peace be upon him) ) advised me to observe three things: (1) to fast three days a month; (2) to pray two rak`at of Duha prayer (forenoon prayer); and (3) to pray witr before sleeping
events.title: Advice of the Prophet ﷺ

guides: Raise your hands and say: Allah is the Greatest.
سُبْحانَكَ اللَّهُمَّ وَبِحَمْدِكَ، وَتَبارَكَ اسْمُكَ، وَتَعَالَى جَدُّكَ، وَلاَ إِلَهَ غَيْرُكَ
Subhanakal-lahumma wabihamdika watabarakas-muka wataʿala jadduka wala ilaha ghayruk
Say quietly: How perfect You are O Allah, and I praise You. Blessed be Your name, and lofty is Your position and none has the right to be worshipped except You.

بِسْمِ اللَّهِ الرَّحْمَٰنِ الرَّحِيمِ ۝ الْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ رَبِّ الْعَالَمِينَ ۝ الرَّحْمَٰنِ الرَّحِيمِ ۝ مَالِكِ يَوْمِ الدِّينِ ۝ إِيَّاكَ نَعْبُدُ وَإِيَّاكَ نَسْتَعِينُ ۝ اهْدِنَا الصِّرَاطَ الْمُسْتَقِيمَ ۝ صِرَاطَ الَّذِينَ أَنْعَمْتَ عَلَيْهِمْ غَيْرِ الْمَغْضُوبِ عَلَيْهِمْ وَلَا الضَّالِّينَ

Then recite another surah or some verses in the first two rak'ahs. In the name of Allāh, the Entirely Merciful, the Especially Merciful. [All] praise is [due] to Allāh, Lord of the worlds - The Entirely Merciful, the Especially Merciful, Sovereign of the Day of Recompense. It is You we worship and You we ask for help. Guide us to the straight path - The path of those upon whom You have bestowed favor, not of those who have earned [Your] anger or of those who are astray.
Say Allahu Akbar and bow, then say (3 times or more): How perfect my Lord is, The Supreme.’
May Allah answer he who praises Him. This supplication is to be made while rising.
Say Allahu Akbar and prostrate, then say (3 times or more): How perfect my Lord is, The Most High.’
رَبِّ اغْفِرْ لِي، رَبِّ اغْفِرْ لِي
My Lord forgive me, My Lord forgive me.

التَّحِيَّاتُ لِلَّهِ، وَالصَّلَواتُ، وَالطَّيِّباتُ، السَّلاَمُ عَلَيْكَ أَيُّهَا النَّبِيُّ وَرَحْمَةُ اللَّهِ وَبَرَكَاتُهُ، السَّلاَمُ عَلَيْنَا وَعَلَى عِبَادِ اللَّهِ الصَّالِحِينَ. أَشْهَدُ أَنْ لاَ إِلَهَ إِلاَّ اللَّهُ وَأَشْهَدُ أَنَّ مُحَمَّداً عَبْدُهُ وَرَسولُهُ

Attahiyyatu lillahi wassalawatu wattayyibat, assalamu ʿalayka ayyuhan-nabiyyu warahmatul-lahi wabarakatuh, assalamu ʿalayna waʿala ʿibadil-lahis-saliheen Ash-hadu an la ilaha illal-lah, wa-ashhadu anna Muhammadan ʿabduhu warasooluh

At-tahiyyat is for Allah. All acts of worship and good deeds are for Him. Peace and the mercy and blessings of Allah be upon you O Prophet. Peace be upon us and all of Allah’s righteous servants. I bear witness that none has the right to be worshipped except Allah and I bear witness that Muhammad is His slave and Messenger. At-tahiyyat: all words which indicate the glorification of Allah. His eternal existence, His perfection and His sovereignty.

اللَّهُمَّ صَلِّ عَلَى مُحَمَّدٍ، وَعَلَى آلِ مُحَمَّدٍ، كَمَا صَلَّيتَ عَلَى إِبْرَاهِيمَ، وَعَلَى آلِ إِبْرَاهِيمَ، إِنَّكَ حَمِيدٌ مَجِيدٌ، اللَّهُمَّ بَارِكْ عَلَى مُحَمَّدٍ وَعَلَى آلِ مُحَمَّدٍ، كَمَا بَارَكْتَ عَلَى إِبْرَاهِيمَ وَعَلَى آلِ إِبْرَاهِيمَ، إِنَّكَ حَمِيدٌ مَجِيدٌ

Allahumma salli ʿala Muhammad, wa-ʿala ali Muhammad, kama sallayta ʿala Ibraheema wa-ʿala ali Ibraheem, innaka Hameedun Majeed, allahumma barik ʿala Muhammad, wa-ʿala ali Muhammad, kama barakta ʿala Ibraheema wa-ʿala ali Ibraheem, innaka Hameedun Majeed

In the last sitting, after the Tashahhud: O Allah, send prayers upon Muhammad and the followers of Muhammad, just as You sent prayers upon Ibraheem and upon the followers of Ibraheem. Verily, You are full of praise and majesty. O Allah, send blessings upon Mohammad and upon the family of Muhammad, just as You sent blessings upon Ibraheem and upon the family of Ibraheem. Verily, You are full of praise and majesty. send prayers: praise and exalt him in the highest and superior of gatherings: that of the closest angels to Allah (al) has been translated in it’s broadest sense: some scholars are of the view that the meaning here is more specific and that it means: his followers from among his family.
اللَّهُــمَّ إِنِّي أَعُوذُ بِكَ مِنْ عَذَابِ الْقَبْرِ، وَمِنْ عَذَابِ جَهَنَّمَ، وَمِنْ فِتْنَةِ الْمَحْيَا وَالْمَمَاتِ، وَمِنْ شَرِّ فِتْنَةِ الْمَسِيحِ الدَّجَّالِ
Allahumma innee aʿoothu bika min ʿathabil-qabr, wamin ʿathabi jahannam, wamin fitnatil-mahya walmamat, wamin shari fitnatil-maseehid-dajjal

O Allah, I take refuge in You from the punishment of the grave, from the torment of the Fire, from the trials and tribulations of life and death and from the evil affliction of Al-Maseeh Ad-Dajjal. Al-Maseeh Ad-Dajjal: among the great signs of the last hour and the greatest trials to befall mankind, which every Prophet has warned about. Most of mankind will follow him. He will appear from Asbahan, Iran at the time when the Muslims will conquer Constantinople. He will be given special powers and will make the truth seem false and vice versa. He will claim to be righteous and then he will claim prophethood and finally, divinity. From his features is that he will be blind in his right eye which is a definite proof that contradicts his claim to be Allah as it is a sign of imperfection. The word Kafir will be written between his eyes which every believer, literate or illiterate will recognise.

Turn to the right, then to the left. The Prophet (peace be upon him) used to give the salutation to his left and right sides until the whiteness of his cheek was seen, (saying: "Peace be upon you, and mercy of Allah" twice.
أَسْتَغْفِرُ اللَّهَ اللَّهُمَّ أَنْتَ السَّلاَمُ، وَمِنْكَ السَّلاَمُ، تَبَارَكْتَ يَا ذَا الْجَلاَلِ وَالْإِكْرَامِ
Astaghfirul-lah Allahumma antas-salam waminkas-salam, tabarakta ya thal-jalali wal-ikram

I ask Allah for forgiveness. (O Allah, You are As-Salam and from You is all peace, blessed are You, O Possessor of majesty and honour. AS-Salam: The One Who is free from all defects and deficiencies.)
Stand facing the Qibla, behind the imam, and say Allahu Akbar. The funeral prayer has four takbirs, no ruku and no sujood.

بِسْمِ اللَّهِ الرَّحْمَٰنِ الرَّحِيمِ ۝ الْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ رَبِّ الْعَالَمِينَ ۝ الرَّحْمَٰنِ الرَّحِيمِ ۝ مَالِكِ يَوْمِ الدِّينِ ۝ إِيَّاكَ نَعْبُدُ وَإِيَّاكَ نَسْتَعِينُ ۝ اهْدِنَا الصِّرَاطَ الْمُسْتَقِيمَ ۝ صِرَاطَ الَّذِينَ أَنْعَمْتَ عَلَيْهِمْ غَيْرِ الْمَغْضُوبِ عَلَيْهِمْ وَلَا الضَّالِّينَ

Recite Al-Fatiha. In the name of Allāh, the Entirely Merciful, the Especially Merciful. [All] praise is [due] to Allāh, Lord of the worlds - The Entirely Merciful, the Especially Merciful, Sovereign of the Day of Recompense. It is You we worship and You we ask for help. Guide us to the straight path - The path of those upon whom You have bestowed favor, not of those who have earned [Your] anger or of those who are astray.
فَقَرَأَ بِفَاتِحَةِ الْكِتَابِ قَالَ لِيَعْلَمُوا أَنَّهَا سُنَّةٌ
I offered the funeral prayer behind Ibn `Abbas and he recited Al-Fatiha and said, "You should know that it (i.e. recitation of Al-Fatiha) is the tradition of the Prophet Muhammad ((peace be upon him)
After the 2nd Takbir: blessings on the Prophet ﷺ

اللَّهُمَّ صَلِّ عَلَى مُحَمَّدٍ، وَعَلَى آلِ مُحَمَّدٍ، كَمَا صَلَّيتَ عَلَى إِبْرَاهِيمَ، وَعَلَى آلِ إِبْرَاهِيمَ، إِنَّكَ حَمِيدٌ مَجِيدٌ، اللَّهُمَّ بَارِكْ عَلَى مُحَمَّدٍ وَعَلَى آلِ مُحَمَّدٍ، كَمَا بَارَكْتَ عَلَى إِبْرَاهِيمَ وَعَلَى آلِ إِبْرَاهِيمَ، إِنَّكَ حَمِيدٌ مَجِيدٌ

Allahumma salli ʿala Muhammad, wa-ʿala ali Muhammad, kama sallayta ʿala Ibraheema wa-ʿala ali Ibraheem, innaka Hameedun Majeed, allahumma barik ʿala Muhammad, wa-ʿala ali Muhammad, kama barakta ʿala Ibraheema wa-ʿala ali Ibraheem, innaka Hameedun Majeed

O Allah, send prayers upon Muhammad and the followers of Muhammad, just as You sent prayers upon Ibraheem and upon the followers of Ibraheem. Verily, You are full of praise and majesty. O Allah, send blessings upon Mohammad and upon the family of Muhammad, just as You sent blessings upon Ibraheem and upon the family of Ibraheem. Verily, You are full of praise and majesty. send prayers: praise and exalt him in the highest and superior of gatherings: that of the closest angels to Allah (al) has been translated in it’s broadest sense: some scholars are of the view that the meaning here is more specific and that it means: his followers from among his family.
After the 3rd Takbir: dua for the deceased

اللَّهُمَّ اغْفِرْ لَهُ وَارْحَمْهُ، وَعَافِهِ، وَاعْفُ عَنْهُ، وَأَكْرِمْ نُزُلَهُ، وَوَسِّعْ مُدْخَلَهُ، وَاغْسِلْهُ بِالْمَاءِ وَالثَّلْجِ وَالْبَرَدِ، وَنَقِّهِ مِنَ الْخَطَايَا كَمَا نَقَّيْتَ الثَّوْبَ الأَبْيَضَ مِنَ الدَّنَسِ، وَأَبْدِلْهُ دَاراً خَيْراً مِنْ دَارِهِ، وَأَهْلاً خَيْراً مِنْ أَهْلِهِ، وَزَوْجَاً خَيْراً مِنْ زَوْجِهِ، وَأَدْخِلْهُ الْجَنَّةَ، وَأَعِذْهُ مِنْ عَذَابِ القَبْرِ وَعَذَابِ النَّارِ

Allahummagh-fir lahu warhamh, waʿafihi, waʿfu ʿanh, wa-akrim nuzulah, wawassiʿ mudkhalah, waghsilhu bilma-i waththalji walbarad, wanaqqihi minal-khataya kama naqqaytath-thawbal-abyada minad-danas, wa-abdilhu daran khayran min darih, wa-ahlan khayran min ahlih wazawjan khayran min zawjih, wa-adkhilhul-jannah, wa-aʿithhu min ʿathabil-qabr, waʿathabin-nar

O Allah, forgive and have mercy upon him, excuse him and pardon him, and make honourable his reception. Expand his entry, and cleanse him with water, snow, and ice, and purify him of sin as a white robe is purified of filth. Exchange his home for a better home, and his family for a better family, and his spouse for a better spouse. Admit him into the Garden, protect him from the punishment of the grave and the torment of the Fire.

اللَّهُمَّ أَعِذْهُ مِنْ عَذَابِ القَبْرِ
اللَّهُمَّ اجْعَلْهُ فَرَطاً وَذُخْراً لِوَالِدَيْهِ، وَشَفِيعاً مُجَاباً، اللَّهُمَّ ثَقِّلْ بِهِ مَوَازِينَهُمَا، وَأَعْظِمْ بِهِ أُجورَهُمَا، وَأَلْحِقْهُ بِصَالِحِ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ، وَاجْعَلْهُ فِي كَفَالَةِ إِبْرَاهِيمَ، وَقِهِ بِرَحْمَتِكَ عَذَابَ الْجَحِيمِ، وَأَبْدِلْهُ دَاراً خَيْراً مِنْ دَارِهِ، وَأَهْلاً خَيْراً مِنْ أَهْلِهِ، اللَّهُمَّ اغْفِرْ لِأَسْلاَفِنَا، وَأَفْرَاطِنَا، وَمَنْ سَبَقَنَا بِالْإِيمَانِ

Allaahumma 'a'ith-hu min 'athaabil-qabri Allahummaj-ʿalhu faratan, wathukhran liwalidayh, washafeeʿan mujaban Allahumma thaqqil bihi mawazeenahuma wa-aʿthim bihi ojoorahuma, wa-alhiqhu bisalihil-mu'mineen, wajʿalhu fee kafalati Ibraheem, waqihi birahmatika ʿathabal-jaheem, wa 'abdilhu daaran khayran min daarihi, wa 'ahlan khayran min 'ahlihi, Allaahum-maghfir li'aslaafinaa, wa afraatinaa wa man sabaqanaa bil'eemaan

O Allah, protect him from the torment of the grave . [it is also good to say] O Allah, make him a precursor, a forerunner and a treasure for his parents and an answered intercessor. O Allah, make him weigh heavily in their scales (of good) and magnify their reward. Make him join the righteous of the believers. Place him in the care of Ibrahim. Save him by Your mercy from the torment of Hell. Give him a home better than his home and a family better than his family. O Allah, forgive those who have gone (i.e. passed away) before us, our children lost (by death), and those who have preceded us in Faith.
Make a short dua or pause briefly, then end with Salam to the right.
وَإِذَا ضَرَبْتُمْ فِي الْأَرْضِ فَلَيْسَ عَلَيْكُمْ جُنَاحٌ أَن تَقْصُرُوا مِنَ الصَّلَاةِ إِنْ خِفْتُمْ أَن يَفْتِنَكُمُ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا إِنَّ الْكَافِرِينَ كَانُوا لَكُمْ عَدُوًّا مُّبِينًا

And when you travel throughout the land, there is no blame upon you for shortening the prayer, [especially] if you fear that those who disbelieve may disrupt [or attack] you. Indeed, the disbelievers are ever to you a clear enemy.
صَدَقَةٌ تَصَدَّقَ اللَّهُ بِهَا عَلَيْكُمْ فَاقْبَلُوا صَدَقَتَهُ

I told 'Umar b. al-Khattab that Allah had said:" You may shorten the prayer only if you fear that those who are unbelievers may afflict you" (Qur'an, iv. 101), whereas the people are now safe. He replied: I wondered about it in the same way as you wonder about it, so I asked the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) about it and he said: It is an act of charity which Allah has done to you, so accept His charity
خَرَجْنَا مَعَ النَّبِيِّ ﷺ مِنَ الْمَدِينَةِ إِلَى مَكَّةَ، فَكَانَ يُصَلِّي رَكْعَتَيْنِ رَكْعَتَيْنِ حَتَّى رَجَعْنَا إِلَى الْمَدِينَةِ
We traveled with the Prophet (peace be upon him) from Medina to Mecca and offered two rak`at (for every prayer) till we returned to Medina.
الصَّلاَةُ أَوَّلُ مَا فُرِضَتْ رَكْعَتَيْنِ فَأُقِرَّتْ صَلاَةُ السَّفَرِ، وَأُتِمَّتْ صَلاَةُ الْحَضَرِ
When the prayers were first enjoined they were of two rak`at each. Later the prayer in a journey was kept as it was but the prayers for non-travelers were completed.

كَانَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ ﷺ إِذَا ارْتَحَلَ قَبْلَ أَنْ تَزِيغَ الشَّمْسُ أَخَّرَ الظُّهْرَ إِلَى وَقْتِ الْعَصْرِ ثُمَّ نَزَلَ فَجَمَعَ بَيْنَهُمَا فَإِنْ زَاغَتِ الشَّمْسُ قَبْلَ أَنْ يَرْتَحِلَ صَلَّى الظُّهْرَ ثُمَّ رَكِبَ

When the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) set out on a journey before the sun declined (from the meridian), he delayed the noon prayer till the afternoon prayer, and then dismounted (his ride) and combined them (noon and afternoon prayers), but if the sun had declined before his setting out on a journey, he observed the noon prayer and then mounted (the ride)
While travelling, Dhuhr, Asr and Isha can be shortened to 2 rak'ahs. Fajr stays 2 and Maghrib stays 3. Dhuhr with Asr, and Maghrib with Isha, may be combined.

اللَّهُ أَكْبَرُ، اللَّهُ أَكْبَرُ، اللَّهُ أَكْبَرُ، سُبْحَانَ الَّذِي سَخَّرَ لَنَا هَذَا وَمَا كُنَّا لَهُ مُقْرِنِينَ ۝ وَإِنَّا إِلَى رَبِّنَا لَمُنقَلِبُونَ اللَّهُمَّ إِنّا نَسْأَلُكَ فِي سَفَرِنَا هَذَا البِرَّ وَالتَّقْوَى، وَمِنَ الْعَمَلِ مَا تَرْضَى، اللَّهُمَّ هَوِّنْ عَلَيْنَا سَفَرَنَا هَذَا وَاطْوِ عَنَّا بُعْدَهُ، اللَّهُمَّ أَنْتَ الصَّاحِبُ فِي السَّفَرِ، وَالْخَليفَةُ فِي الْأَهْلِ، اللَّهُمَّ إِنِّي أَعُوذُ بِكَ مِنْ وَعْثَاءِ السَّفَرِ، وَكَآبَةِ الْمَنْظَرِ، وَسُوءِ الْمُنْقَلَبِ فِي الْمَالِ وَالْأَهْلِ

Allahu akbar, Allahu akbar, Allahu akbar, subhanal-lathee sakhkhara lana hatha wama kunna lahu muqrineen, wa-inna ila rabbina lamunqaliboon, allahumma inna nas-aluka fee safarina hatha albirra wattaqwa, waminal-ʿamali ma tarda, allahumma hawwin ʿalayna safarana hatha, watwi ʿanna buʿdah, allahumma antas-sahibu fis-safar, walkhaleefatu fil-ahl, allahumma innee aʿoothu bika min waʿtha-is-safar, waka-abatil-manthar, wasoo-il-munqalabi fil-mali wal-ahl Ayiboona, ta-iboona, ʿabidoona, lirabbina hamidoon

Allah is the greatest, Allah is the greatest, Allah is the greatest, How perfect He is, The One Who has placed this (transport) at our service, and we ourselves would not have been capable of that, and to our Lord is our final destiny. O Allah, we ask You for birr and taqwa in this journey of ours, and we ask You for deeds which please You. O Allah, facilitate our journey and let us cover it’s distance quickly. O Allah, You are The Companion on the journey and The Successor over the family, O Allah, I take refuge with You from the difficulties of travel, from having a change of hearts and being in a bad predicament, and I take refuge in You from an ill fated outcome with wealth and family.
لَبَّيْكَ اللَّهُمَّ لَبَّيْكَ، لَبَّيْكَ لاَ شَرِيكَ لَكَ لَبَّيْكَ، إِنَّ الْحَمْدَ، وَالنِّعْمَةَ، لَكَ وَالْمُلْكَ، لاَ شَرِيكَ لَكَ
Labbaykal-lahumma labbayk, labbayka la shareeka laka labbayk, innal-hamda wanniʿmata laka walmulk, la shareeka lak

Enter ihram at the miqat with the intention for Umrah and say the Talbiyah often: Here I am O Allah, (in response to Your call), here I am. Here I am, You have no partner, here I am. Verily all praise, grace and sovereignty belong to You. You have no partner.
Start Tawaf at the Black Stone
طَافَ النَّبيُّ ﷺ بِالْبَيْتِ عَلَى بَعِيرٍ كُلَّمَا أَتَى الرُّكْنَ أَشَارَ إِلَيْهِ بِشَيْءٍ عِنْدَهُ وَكَبَّرَ

Go around the Ka'bah 7 times, starting at the Black Stone. Each time you pass the Black Stone, point to it and say Allahu Akbar. The Prophet (peace be upon him) circled the KaAAbah on a camel, every time he reached the black stone he would point to it with his staff and say: (Allah is the greatest)
Between the Yemeni Corner and the Black Stone
رَبَّنَا آتِنَا فِي الدُّنْيَا حَسَنَةً وَفِي الْآخِرَةِ حَسَنَةً وَقِنَا عَذَابَ النَّارِ
Rabbana atina fee alddunya hasanatan wafee al-akhirati hasanatan waqina ʿathaba alnnar Al-Baqarah

The Prophet (peace be upon him) used to say between the Yemeni corner and the black stone: (O our Lord, grant us the best in this life and the best in the next life, and protect us from the punishment of the Fire.)

وَإِذْ جَعَلْنَا الْبَيْتَ مَثَابَةً لِّلنَّاسِ وَأَمْنًا وَاتَّخِذُوا مِن مَّقَامِ إِبْرَاهِيمَ مُصَلًّى وَعَهِدْنَا إِلَىٰ إِبْرَاهِيمَ وَإِسْمَاعِيلَ أَن طَهِّرَا بَيْتِيَ لِلطَّائِفِينَ وَالْعَاكِفِينَ وَالرُّكَّعِ السُّجُودِ

Pray two rak'ahs behind Maqam Ibrahim if you can. And [mention] when We made the House [i.e., the Kaʿbah] a place of return for the people and [a place of] security. And take, [O believers], from the standing place of Abraham a place of prayer. And We charged Abraham and Ishmael, [saying], "Purify My House for those who perform ṭawāf and those who are staying [there] for worship and those who bow and prostrate [in prayer]."

لاَ إِلَهَ إِلاَّ اللَّهُ وَحْدَهُ لاَ شَرِيكَ لَهُ، لَهُ الْمُلْكُ وَلَهُ الْحَمْدُ وَهُوَ عَلَى كُلِّ شَيْءٍ قَدِيرٌ، لاَ إِلَهَ إِلاَّ اللَّهُ وَحْدَهُ، أَنْجَزَ وَعْدَهُ، وَنَصَرَ عَبْدَهُ، وَهَزَمَ الْأَحْزَابَ وَحْدَهُ، ثُمَّ دَعَا بَيْنَ ذلكَ. قَالَ مِثْلَ هَذَا ثَلاَثَ مَرَّاتٍ
فَفَعَلَ عَلَى الْمَرْوَةِ كَمَا فَعَلَ عَلَى الصَّفَا

Innas-safa wa-almarwata min shaʿa-iri Allah … Abda-o bima badaal-lahu bih Allahu akbar, Allahu akbar, Allahu akbar after each time La ilaha illal-lahu wahdahu la shareeka lah, lahul-mulku walahul-hamd, wahuwa ʿala kulli shayin qadeer, la ilaha illal-lahu wahdah, anjaza waʿdah, wanasara ʿabdah, wahazamal -ahzaba wahdah

Walk 7 times between Safa and Marwah, starting at Safa. None has the right to be worshipped except Allah, alone, without partner.To Him belongs all sovereignty and praise and He is over all things amnipotent. None has the right to be worshipped except Allah alone. He fulfilled His promise, aided His Servant and single-handedly defeated the allies.
Safa and Marwah in the Quran
إِنَّ الصَّفَا وَالْمَرْوَةَ مِن شَعَائِرِ اللَّهِ فَمَنْ حَجَّ الْبَيْتَ أَوِ اعْتَمَرَ فَلَا جُنَاحَ عَلَيْهِ أَن يَطَّوَّفَ بِهِمَا وَمَن تَطَوَّعَ خَيْرًا فَإِنَّ اللَّهَ شَاكِرٌ عَلِيمٌ

Indeed, aṣ-Ṣafā and al-Marwah are among the symbols of Allāh. So whoever makes ḥajj [pilgrimage] to the House or performs ʿumrah - there is no blame upon him for walking between them. And whoever volunteers good - then indeed, Allāh is Appreciative and Knowing.
Men shave the head or trim the hair; women trim a fingertip length. Your Umrah is complete.
8th Dhul Hijjah: Ihram and go to Mina
لَبَّيْكَ اللَّهُمَّ لَبَّيْكَ، لَبَّيْكَ لاَ شَرِيكَ لَكَ لَبَّيْكَ، إِنَّ الْحَمْدَ، وَالنِّعْمَةَ، لَكَ وَالْمُلْكَ، لاَ شَرِيكَ لَكَ
Labbaykal-lahumma labbayk, labbayka la shareeka laka labbayk, innal-hamda wanniʿmata laka walmulk, la shareeka lak

Enter ihram for Hajj, go to Mina and say the Talbiyah often. Here I am O Allah, (in response to Your call), here I am. Here I am, You have no partner, here I am. Verily all praise, grace and sovereignty belong to You. You have no partner.
لاَ إِلَهَ إِلاَّ اللَّهُ وَحْدَهُ لاَ شَرِيكَ لَهُ، لَهُ الْمُلْكُ وَلَهُ الْحَمْدُ وَهُوَ عَلَى كُلِّ شَيْءٍ قَدِيرٌ
La ilaha illal-lahu wahdahu la shareeka lah, lahul-mulku walahul-hamd, wahuwa ʿala kulli shayin qadeer

Stand at Arafah from after midday until sunset, busy with dua and dhikr. The best dua is: None has the right to be worshipped except Allah, alone, without partner. To Him belongs all praise and sovereignty and He is over all things omnipotent.

رَكِبَ النَّبِيُّ ﷺ الْقَصْوَاءَ حَتَّى أَتَى الْمَشْعَرَ الْحَرَامَ فَاسْتَقْبَلَ الْقِبْلَةَ فَدَعَاهُ، وَكَبَّرَهُ، وَهَللَّهُ، وَوَحَّدَهُ فَلَمْ يَزَلْ وَاقِفاً حَتَّى أَسْفَرَ جِدَّاً فَدَفَعَ قَبْلَ أَنْ تَطْلُعَ الشَّمسُ

After sunset go to Muzdalifah, pray Maghrib and Isha, stay the night, and after Fajr remember Allah: The Prophet rode his camel, Al-Qaswa, until he reached the sacred area (Al-Mash aril Haraam). Then he faced the Qiblah and invoked Allah, and repeatedly said the words: Allaahu Akbar (Allah is the Most Great), Allaahu Ahad (Allah is One) and Laa ilaaha illallaah (There is none worthy of worship but Allah). He remained stationary until the sky became yellow with the dawn, and then pressed on before sunrise.

لَيْسَ عَلَيْكُمْ جُنَاحٌ أَن تَبْتَغُوا فَضْلًا مِّن رَّبِّكُمْ فَإِذَا أَفَضْتُم مِّنْ عَرَفَاتٍ فَاذْكُرُوا اللَّهَ عِندَ الْمَشْعَرِ الْحَرَامِ وَاذْكُرُوهُ كَمَا هَدَاكُمْ وَإِن كُنتُم مِّن قَبْلِهِ لَمِنَ الضَّالِّينَ

There is no blame upon you for seeking bounty from your Lord [during ḥajj]. But when you depart from ʿArafāt, remember Allāh at al-Mashʿar al-Ḥarām. And remember Him, as He has guided you, for indeed, you were before that among those astray.

يُكَبِّرُ كُلَّمَا رَمَى بِحَصَاةٍ عِنْدَ الْجِمَارِ الثَّلاَثِ، ثُمَّ يَتَقَدَّمُ، ويَقِفُ يَدْعُو مُسْتَقْبِلَ الْقِبلَةِ، رَافِعاً يَدَيْهِ بَعْدَ الْجَمْرَةِ الْأُولَى وَالثَّانِيَةِ. أَمَّا جَمْرَةُ الْعَقَبَةِ فَيَرْمِيهَا وَيُكَبِّرُ عِنْدَ كُلِّ حَصَاةٍ وَيَنْصَرِفُ وَلاَ يَقِفُ عِنْدَهَا

Throw 7 pebbles at Jamrat al-Aqabah, saying with each one: The Prophet (peace be upon him) said Allaahu 'Akbar (Allah is the Most Great) with each pebble he threw at the three pillars. Then he went forward, stood facing the Qiblah and raised his hands and called upon Allah. That was after (stoning) the first and second pillar As for the third, he stoned it and called out Allahu Akbar with every pebble he threw but when he was finished he left without standing at it (for supplications).
بِسْمِ اللَّهِ وَاللَّهُ أَكْبَرُ اللَّهُمَّ مِنْكَ وَلَكَ اللَّهُمَّ تَقَبَّلْ مِنِّي
Bismil-lah wallahu akbar, allahumma minka walak, allahumma taqabbal minnee
Then sacrifice your animal, saying: In the name of Allah, and Allah is the greatest. O Allah, (it is) from You and belongs to You, O Allah, accept this from me.
10th: Shave or trim, then Tawaf al-Ifadah and Sa'i
Men shave or trim, women trim. Then do Tawaf al-Ifadah and the Sa'i of Hajj.
Stay in Mina and stone all three Jamarat each day after midday. The days of Tashriq are the days of eating and drinking
Before leaving Makkah, make the farewell Tawaf.

prophet_sections: Allah told the angels that He would place a successor (khalifah) on the earth. The angels asked whether He would place there one who would cause corruption, while they glorified Him. Allah said, "I know what you do not know." He taught Adam the names of all things. When the angels could not tell them, Adam told them, and Allah's wisdom became clear to them.

Allah commanded the angels to prostrate to Adam. They all did, except Iblees. Out of arrogance he said, "I am better than him. You created me from fire and created him from clay." He was expelled, and he swore to mislead Adam's children from every direction until the Day of Resurrection. Allah warned that whoever follows him will fill Hell.

Adam and his wife lived in the Garden and could eat freely from it, but were told not to approach one tree. Shaytan whispered to them and swore that he was a sincere adviser. They ate from the tree, their nakedness became apparent to them, and they began covering themselves with leaves of the Garden.

Adam and his wife did not argue or blame others. They said: "Our Lord, we have wronged ourselves, and if You do not forgive us and have mercy upon us, we will surely be among the losers." Adam received words from his Lord and Allah accepted his repentance — He is the Accepting of repentance, the Merciful. They were sent down to the earth, with the promise that guidance would come, and whoever follows it will not fear or grieve.

Two sons of Adam each offered a sacrifice. It was accepted from one and not from the other. The one whose offering was rejected threatened his brother, who replied that Allah accepts only from the righteous and that he would not raise his hand to kill. The jealous brother killed him, and then Allah sent a crow scratching the ground to show him how to bury his brother. He became one of the regretful.
Allah mentions Al-Yasa' among those He favoured over the worlds and among the outstanding. The Quran gives no further detail.
Ayyub was tested with severe harm. He called to his Lord: "Indeed, adversity has touched me, and You are the most merciful of the merciful."

Allah answered him: "Strike the ground with your foot; this is a cool spring for washing and drinking." Allah removed his harm and gave him back his family and the like of them with them, as a mercy and a reminder. Allah said: "Indeed, We found him patient. An excellent servant. Indeed, he was one repeatedly turning back to Allah."
With the small army of Talut, Dawud killed Jalut (Goliath). Allah gave him kingship and wisdom and taught him from what He willed.
Allah gave Dawud the Zabur (Psalms). The mountains and the birds glorified Allah with him in the evening and the morning.
Allah softened iron for him and taught him to make coats of armour, saying: "Do righteous deeds."

Two disputants climbed into his prayer chamber. After judging, Dawud realised he was being tested; he asked forgiveness, fell down bowing and turned in repentance. Allah told him: "We have made you a successor on earth, so judge between people in truth and do not follow your desire."
Among the patient and the best
Allah mentions Dhul-Kifl together with Ismail and Idris as being among the patient, admitted into His mercy, and among the outstanding. The Quran gives no further detail, so we add none.
Musa asked Allah to make his brother Harun his helper, because Harun was more eloquent. Allah granted his request and sent them both to Pharaoh, telling them to speak to him gently.

While Musa was away, Harun warned the people that the calf was a trial and told them to follow him and obey his order. They refused. When Musa returned and seized him in anger, Harun explained that he had feared being blamed for dividing the Children of Israel.

Allah sent Hud to his people, ʿAad, a powerful nation who built landmarks on every height for vanity and great fortresses as if they would live forever. Hud told them to worship Allah alone, to fear Him, and reminded them of His blessings: cattle, children, gardens and springs.

They said: "It is all the same to us whether you advise us or not." They demanded the punishment he warned them of, and accused him of foolishness. Hud replied that he was a sincere, trustworthy messenger and that he relied upon Allah, his Lord and theirs.

When they saw a cloud approaching their valleys, they said: "This is a cloud bringing us rain!" But it was what they had sought to hasten: a wind carrying a painful punishment. It raged against them for seven nights and eight days, leaving them like hollow trunks of palm trees. Allah saved Hud and those who believed with him by His mercy.

Ibrahim saw his father and his people worshipping idols and the stars. He reasoned with them: a star sets, the moon sets, the sun sets — "I do not like those that disappear." He turned his face to the One who created the heavens and the earth, inclining to the truth, and he was not of those who associate partners with Allah.

Ibrahim called his father with great gentleness: "O my father, why do you worship that which does not hear and does not see?" His father threatened to stone him. Ibrahim answered, "Peace be upon you. I will ask forgiveness for you of my Lord."

While his people were away, Ibrahim broke their idols into pieces, except the largest. When they asked who had done this, he said, "Rather, this — the largest of them — did it, so ask them, if they can speak." They were confounded, then turned back to their stubbornness.
They said, "Burn him and support your gods." Allah said: "O fire, be coolness and safety upon Ibrahim." Their plan failed and they became the losers.

A king argued with Ibrahim about his Lord. Ibrahim said, "My Lord is the one who gives life and causes death." The king said, "I give life and cause death." Ibrahim said, "Allah brings the sun from the east; so bring it from the west." The disbeliever was left speechless.

Ibrahim settled some of his family in an uncultivated valley near Allah's sacred House and prayed that hearts would incline towards them and that they would be provided with fruits. Later, he and Ismail raised the foundations of the House, praying: "Our Lord, accept this from us."

Ibrahim saw in a dream that he was sacrificing his son. His son said, "O my father, do as you are commanded. You will find me, if Allah wills, of the steadfast." When they had both submitted, Allah called out to him that he had fulfilled the vision, and ransomed the son with a great sacrifice.
Angels came to Ibrahim as guests; he quickly served them a roasted calf. They gave him and his wife the good news of a knowledgeable son, Ishaq, and after him Ya'qub, even though they were old.
Allah took Ibrahim as an intimate friend (khalil), and commanded the believers to follow the way of Ibrahim, inclining to the truth.

The Quran tells us only a little about Idris: he was a man of truth and a prophet, and Allah raised him to a high station. He is named among the patient and the righteous whom Allah admitted into His mercy. We do not add stories that are not established.

Ilyas was one of the messengers. He said to his people: "Will you not fear Allah? Do you call upon Ba'l and leave the best of creators — Allah, your Lord and the Lord of your forefathers?" They denied him, except Allah's chosen servants. Allah left praise of him among later generations.
The angels told Maryam that Allah had chosen her, purified her and chosen her above the women of the worlds, and told her to be devoutly obedient, prostrate and bow with those who bow.

An angel came to her in the form of a man and gave her the news of a pure boy. She asked how, when no man had touched her. He said: "It is easy for your Lord." The pains of birth drove her to the trunk of a palm tree, where she was told to shake it and eat the ripe dates and drink.
When her people accused her, she pointed to the baby. He spoke: "I am the servant of Allah. He has given me the Scripture and made me a prophet... and made me dutiful to my mother."

By Allah's permission he made a bird from clay and breathed into it, healed the blind and the leper, and brought the dead to life. His disciples asked for a table spread with food from heaven, and he prayed for it.

They did not kill him, nor did they crucify him, but it was made to appear so to them. Rather, Allah raised him to Himself. 'Isa never told people to worship him; he said, "Worship Allah, my Lord and your Lord." He gave the good news of a messenger to come after him named Ahmad.
The example of 'Isa with Allah is like that of Adam: He created him from dust and said to him "Be," and he was.

Angels brought Ibrahim and his wife the good news of Ishaq when they were old. She was amazed. They said, "Are you amazed at the decree of Allah? The mercy of Allah and His blessings be upon you, people of the house."
Allah made Ishaq and Ya'qub righteous leaders, guiding by His command, and inspired them to do good deeds, establish prayer and give zakah.
Allah praised Ismail: he was true to his promise, a messenger and a prophet. He enjoined prayer and zakah upon his family and was pleasing to his Lord.
Allah names Ismail, together with Idris and Dhul-Kifl, among the patient, whom He admitted into His mercy as righteous.
With his father Ibrahim he raised the foundations of the House, both praying that Allah accept it from them.
Lut believed in Ibrahim, and he said, "I will emigrate for the sake of my Lord."

Lut was sent to a people who committed an immorality that no one in the worlds had done before them: they approached men with desire instead of women, and committed evil openly in their gatherings. He warned them, and they answered, "Expel them from your town; they are people who keep themselves pure."

Angels came to Lut in the form of men. He was distressed for them, and his people rushed towards him. He pleaded with them to fear Allah and not disgrace him with his guests. The angels told him: "We are messengers of your Lord; they will never reach you. Leave with your family during the night, and let none of you look back — except your wife."

At dawn the command came: the town was turned upside down and stones of baked clay rained upon it. Lut and his family were saved, except his wife, who was among those who stayed behind. Her betrayal is given as an example of disbelief.
Muhammad ﷺ is the Messenger of Allah and the seal of the prophets, sent as a mercy to the worlds and to all of mankind. Allah praised his character: "Indeed, you are of a great moral character."
The revelation began with the words: "Read in the name of your Lord who created." The hadith below describes how it began in the cave of Hira.
Allah took His servant by night from al-Masjid al-Haram to al-Masjid al-Aqsa, whose surroundings He blessed, to show him of His signs.
When the disbelievers drove him out, he was one of two in the cave and said to his companion, "Do not grieve; indeed Allah is with us." Allah sent down His tranquillity upon him.

Allah gave the believers victory at Badr when they were few, and later granted a clear conquest. When the help of Allah came and people entered Allah's religion in crowds, he was told to glorify his Lord and seek His forgiveness.

Allah said: "This day I have perfected for you your religion and completed My favour upon you and approved for you Islam as religion." Muhammad ﷺ is a messenger like those before him; he passed away, and the believers remain firm.

Pharaoh was killing the baby boys of the Children of Israel. Allah inspired Musa's mother: put him in a chest and cast it into the river. Pharaoh's household picked him up, and his wife said, "A comfort of the eye for me and for you; do not kill him." Musa refused every wet nurse until his sister guided them to his own mother — so Allah returned him to her.

As a young man Musa struck an Egyptian who was fighting an Israelite, and the man died. Musa repented: "My Lord, I have wronged myself, so forgive me," and Allah forgave him. Warned that the chiefs were plotting to kill him, he fled towards Madyan.

At the well of Madyan he watered the flocks of two women, then sat in the shade praying: "My Lord, I am in need of whatever good You send down to me." One of them came walking shyly to invite him to her father. Musa married one of the daughters and worked for some years.

Travelling with his family, Musa saw a fire on the side of Mount Tur. There he was called: "I am Allah, Lord of the worlds." His staff became a moving snake, his hand came out shining white, and he was sent to Pharaoh. He asked Allah to expand his chest, ease his task and make his brother Harun his helper.

Pharaoh denied the signs and gathered his magicians. They threw their ropes and staffs, which seemed to move. Musa threw his staff and it swallowed what they had faked. The magicians fell down in prostration and believed. Pharaoh threatened them with crucifixion; they said, "Decide whatever you will; you can only decide for this worldly life."

Allah sent plagues upon Pharaoh's people — floods, locusts, lice, frogs and blood — but they remained arrogant. Musa left by night with the Children of Israel. Trapped at the sea, his people said, "We will surely be overtaken!" Musa said: "No! My Lord is with me; He will guide me." He struck the sea and it parted. Pharaoh and his army followed and were drowned.

Musa went to meet his Lord for forty nights and received the Tablets. While he was away, as-Samiri made a golden calf and many worshipped it. Musa returned angry and grieved, rebuked them, and the calf was burnt and scattered in the sea.

Musa travelled to meet a servant of Allah who had been given special knowledge. The servant damaged a boat, killed a boy and rebuilt a wall without payment, and Musa could not stay patient. Then he explained: the boat was saved from a tyrant king, the boy's parents would be given a better child, and the wall protected the treasure of two orphans. "I did not do it of my own accord."

Nuh called his people to worship Allah alone for nine hundred and fifty years. He called them night and day, openly and in private. They put their fingers in their ears, covered themselves with their garments and persisted in arrogance.
Nuh told them: "Ask forgiveness of your Lord. Indeed, He is ever a Perpetual Forgiver. He will send rain from the sky upon you in continuing showers and give you increase in wealth and children."

The leaders mocked him and his followers, calling them the lowest of the people. Allah told Nuh that no more of his people would believe, and commanded him to build the Ark under His eyes. Every time the leaders passed by, they ridiculed him.

When Allah's command came, water burst from the earth and poured from the sky. Nuh carried a pair of every kind, his family — except those against whom the word had gone forth — and the believers, who were few. He called to his son, who stayed apart, to come aboard; the son said he would take refuge on a mountain. A wave came between them, and he was among the drowned. Then the earth swallowed its water, the sky withheld its rain, and the Ark came to rest on al-Judiyy.

Nuh called to his Lord about his son. Allah told him that his son was not of his family in faith, for his deeds were unrighteous. Nuh immediately sought refuge in Allah from asking about what he had no knowledge of and asked for forgiveness and mercy.

Salih was sent to his people, Thamud, who carved homes out of the mountains and built palaces on the plains. He reminded them of Allah's blessings and called them to worship Him alone and seek His forgiveness.
They demanded a sign, and Allah sent a she-camel as a clear sign. She had her share of the water on one day and they had theirs on another day. Salih warned them not to harm her.

Nine men in the city spread corruption and plotted to attack Salih and his family at night. The most wretched of them hamstrung the camel, and they arrogantly defied their Lord's command. Salih told them to enjoy themselves for three days. Then the earthquake and the blast seized them and they lay fallen in their homes. Salih and the believers were saved.
Shu'ayb was sent to Madyan. Besides calling them to worship Allah alone, he told them: give full measure and weight, do not deprive people of what is theirs, and do not cause corruption on earth.

They mocked him: "Does your prayer command you that we should leave what our fathers worshipped, or stop doing what we please with our wealth?" He replied: "I only intend reform as much as I am able. My success is only through Allah. Upon Him I have relied and to Him I return."
They threatened to drive him and the believers out. When the command came, the blast and the earthquake seized the wrongdoers, and Allah saved Shu'ayb and those who believed with him.
Sulayman inherited from Dawud. He was taught the speech of birds and given from everything. Allah made the wind subject to him, and jinn worked for him by his Lord's permission.

His army reached the valley of the ants, and an ant warned the others to go into their homes so they would not be crushed. Sulayman smiled and prayed: "My Lord, enable me to be grateful for Your favour which You have bestowed upon me and my parents, and to do righteousness that pleases You."
The hoopoe and the Queen of Sheba

The hoopoe brought news of a queen and her people who prostrated to the sun. Sulayman sent her a letter beginning "In the name of Allah". Her throne was brought to him in the blink of an eye. When she saw the palace, she said: "My Lord, I have wronged myself, and I submit with Sulayman to Allah, Lord of the worlds."

When Allah decreed his death, nothing showed the jinn except a creature of the earth eating his staff. When he fell, the jinn realised that had they known the unseen, they would not have remained in humiliating labour.

Allah said: "O Yahya, take the Scripture with determination." He was given wisdom while still a child, affection and purity from Allah. He was devout, dutiful to his parents, and was neither a tyrant nor disobedient.
He came confirming a word from Allah, as a leader, chaste, and a prophet from among the righteous.
"Peace be upon him the day he was born, the day he dies and the day he is raised alive."
When death approached Ya'qub he asked his sons, "What will you worship after me?" They said, "We will worship your God and the God of your fathers, Ibrahim, Ismail and Ishaq — one God."

When his sons came with Yusuf's shirt stained with false blood, Ya'qub said: "Patience is most fitting, and Allah is the one whose help is sought." Years later, losing another son, he grieved until his eyes turned white, yet he said, "I only complain of my suffering and grief to Allah, and I know from Allah what you do not know." He told his sons never to despair of Allah's mercy.
Yusuf's shirt was placed on his face and his sight returned. He said, "Did I not tell you that I know from Allah what you do not know?"
Yunus left his people in anger and boarded a laden ship. Lots were cast and he was among the losers. A great fish swallowed him while he was blameworthy.

In the darknesses he called out: "There is no deity except You; exalted are You. Indeed, I have been of the wrongdoers." Allah answered him and saved him from distress — "and thus do We save the believers." Had he not been of those who glorify Allah, he would have remained in its belly until the Day of Resurrection.

He was cast onto the open shore while ill, and Allah caused a gourd plant to grow over him. He was sent to a hundred thousand or more, and they believed. His people are the one town that believed and benefited from its faith, so Allah removed the punishment from them.
A lesson for the Prophet ﷺ
Allah told the Prophet ﷺ to be patient and not be like the companion of the fish.
As a boy, Yusuf saw eleven stars, the sun and the moon prostrating to him. His father told him not to tell his brothers, for Shaytan is a clear enemy to man.
His brothers were jealous of their father's love for him. They took him and threw him into a well, then returned weeping with his shirt stained with false blood, claiming a wolf had eaten him.
Travellers found him and sold him for a few coins. A man in Egypt bought him and told his wife to treat him honourably. Allah gave him wisdom and knowledge.

The wife of his master tried to seduce him and closed the doors. Yusuf said, "I seek refuge in Allah," and ran to the door. His shirt torn from the back proved his innocence. When the women of the city gossiped, she invited them; seeing him, they cut their hands in amazement. Yusuf prayed: "My Lord, prison is more beloved to me than what they invite me to."

In prison he called two fellow prisoners to worship Allah alone, then interpreted their dreams. Later the king saw seven fat cows eaten by seven lean ones. Yusuf interpreted it: seven years of plenty followed by seven years of hardship — and advised how to store the grain.
Yusuf refused to leave prison until his innocence was declared. The wife of al-'Aziz admitted the truth. The king made him trusted over the storehouses of the land.

During the famine his brothers came for food, not recognising him. Through a wise plan he kept his younger brother with him. Finally he revealed himself: "I am Yusuf." They admitted their sin, and he said: "No blame upon you today. Allah will forgive you; He is the most merciful of the merciful."

His parents and brothers came to Egypt and bowed before him, and Yusuf said, "O my father, this is the explanation of my dream of before." He thanked Allah and prayed to die as a Muslim and be joined with the righteous.
Zakariyya was the guardian of Maryam. Every time he entered upon her in the prayer chamber he found provision with her. She said: "It is from Allah. Allah provides for whom He wills without account."

Old, with a barren wife, Zakariyya called to his Lord privately: "My Lord, my bones have weakened and my head has filled with white, and never have I been unhappy in my prayer to You." He asked for an heir.
The angels gave him the good news of a son named Yahya, a name given to no one before. As a sign, he would not speak to people for three nights, yet he could glorify Allah morning and evening.
